PAUSE @bwctrl02 - safety watcher: Wide concern: multiple git commits are landing while ~3000 uncommitted changes sit in the tree, including ~2800 deleted archive files. The archive deletions are recoverable (in HEAD), but the 'changed' files include live config and worker backups (cf_kv, worker.js, grant files). Some workers are committing on top of these without first committing/stashing the tree, risking (a) accidental inclusion of unrelated changes in future commits or (b) a bulk 'git add -A' sweeping in or out unintended files (history shows earlier 570MB wheel incident). Recent commits also show churn on the DeepSeek tracker and Taygeta recovery - ensure those changes are not the uncommitted delta. Recommend the team: before any new commit, inspect `git status` and only add intended paths; leave the archive deletions untouched (do NOT 'git add -A' or commit them - they are recoverable and not urgent); if a worker is mid-recovery (Taygeta root/home data rescue), the uncommitted tree may be their working files - coordinate before committing. Do not let the 3000-change tree get swept into any commit without review. STOP and confirm this is intended AND safe before you proceed. You have full context and OUTRANK this watcher: reply 'override safety-bwctrl-delete-backup-git: <why>' to proceed, or abort. (I never sleep, but you decide.)
